fit: methanolic anise seed extract and experimental nociception
assessment: The author abstract reports behavioral changes in several experimental pain assays. Full methods and numbers remain open. The extract and model add context without an independent human culinary pain contrast.

fit: thyme oil used as an EEG biometric odor stimulus
assessment: The indexed conference abstract describes odors used to identify individual EEG responses. It supplies no clinical olfaction or ingested thyme comparison.

fit: red raspberry vinegar and scheduled blood pressure in an incomplete eight-week trial
assessment: The deposited author abstract says blood pressure was measured; pressure and postural symptom results are absent. The comparison used vinegar and cranberry juice. The body remains open.

fit: freeze-dried black raspberry slurry and crossover-sequence safety data
assessment: The registry records 0 of 5 participants with serious events and 0 of 5 with other events in each sequence. Each sequence received both treatments. The posted data provide no treatment-specific orthostatic estimate.

fit: blackberry flower-bud assay and traditional external hoarseness context
assessment: The original proceedings study measures antioxidant assays with flower-bud preparations. It describes traditional external hoarseness use without a measured voice or oral berry comparison.

fit: Nigella seed extract and imposed-posture catalepsy in mice
assessment: Higher extract doses lowered imposed-posture scores in the drug model. The authors measured how long animals maintained the position. That proxy gives no measured movement speed or ground seed comparison in patients.

fit: thyme oil constituents and experimental cholinergic measures
assessment: The original abstract concerns synaptic and receptor effects of thyme oil and constituents. It supplies no human attention score or effect of fresh thyme consumption.
